transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-20
Time: 15:00 PST / 18:00 EST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Chen (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Brightwell Head of ML), Jonas Kramer (Brightwell Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (Brightwell VP Product)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff to align on pilot scope, timeline, network/security requirements for a Private / Dedicated pilot, and next steps. High-level goals: reduce latency for clinical search, integrate embeddings + reranking into existing search, and ensure PHI-safe handling with KMS and audit logs.

Topics:
- Pilot success criteria and timeline
- Deployment mode: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Security: SOC 2, encryption, KMS, SSO, audit logs
- Networking: VPC peering, firewall rules, ports, egress
- Performance benchmarking and telemetry needed
- Roles, onboarding, and admin access

Transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex Rivera from Redwood. Quick intros?
00:07 Maya (Brightwell): Hey, Maya here, head of ML at Brightwell. We're trying to get the search pipeline replaced, so excited to talk.
00:13 Jonas (Brightwell): Jonas, platform, I'll handle the infra side and networking with you.
00:18 Lena (Brightwell): Lena, product. We'll be responsible for rollout and adoption.
00:22 Alex: Great. Priya, Sam, quick intros?
00:25 Priya (Redwood): Priya Nair, solutions engineer, I do deployments and perf.
00:28 Sam (Redwood): Sam Chen, CSM, I'll run onboarding and account setup.
00:33 Alex: Agenda — scope pilot, decide on Dedicated vs Private, collect requirements for security and network, set next steps. Sound good?
00:38 Maya: Yep. We want to run a 6-week pilot, start with hosted to validate quality then move to a private VPC for data residency, ideally by end of Q2. Latency target is under 150ms tail for 256-token prompts. Cost is a factor, too.
00:58 Priya: Cool. Quick clarifying question: when you say "hosted then private", do you mean testing on Redwood hosted endpoints first then shift to Redwood Private VPC, or running a hybrid?
01:08 Maya: Prefer hosted for fast start, then Private VPC for production. We might also evaluate Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput.
01:18 Alex: That matches a common pattern. We'll do a hosted API pilot to iterate on prompts/evals, then move to private once you're happy. For Dedicated vs Private, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools (predictable throughput) while Private gives you a customer-managed VPC control plane. We can propose both for production.
01:33 Jonas: Network-wise, for Private we need VPC peering and a whitelist of egress IPs, plus any firewall ports. We'll need a network prep doc.
01:41 Priya: We'll share a network prep checklist — things like CIDR ranges, peering notes, ports 443 outbound, and a small set of IPs for NAT. I'll make sure it's in the next steps.
01:52 Lena: Security — what about PHI? We need encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also, SSO for admin users.
02:03 Sam: Right, we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. We also provide audit logs and have SOC 2 attestation. I'll share our security pack and KMS guide.
02:14 Maya: Are there any gotchas around KV cache or session persistence that could leak tokens or PHI?
02:21 Priya: We have prefix and KV cache controls; by default we avoid persisting anything unless you opt-in. We'll provide config examples. Note sometimes the auto-transcript refers to KV as KV cash in docs, sorry for the auto transcription.
02:35 Alex: For success criteria you mentioned latency and adoption — can you specify key metrics? QPS peak and average?
02:42 Maya: For search, average QPS 8–12, peak 40 during morning hours. 95th pct latency under 150ms for a 256 token prompt, and embedding generation within 120ms. Also want low token cost per query — we have cost targets.
02:58 Priya: Great. For perf benchmarks we'll need sample payloads and telemetry. If you can share two weeks of search logs and a representative prompt set, we can run a perf profile and recommend batching/quantization profiles.
03:13 Jonas: We'll share log extracts, need to scrub PHI first. Might take a day or two.
03:18 Maya: Yes, security will need to scrub. We'll attach an example anonymizer script.
03:24 Alex: Timeline — pilot start: hosted sandbox by next week, 2-week quality iteration, then private network setup and Dedicated estimate. Is that OK?
03:33 Lena: That works if we can get the security review and network prep done in week 1.
03:38 Sam: We'll aim to provision a sandbox API key and onboarding workspace by 2027-02-23.
03:44 Alex: For Dedicated capacity estimate we'll ask for expected concurrent sessions and token volumes. Jonas, can you provide baseline QPS and avg tokens per request?
03:55 Jonas: We'll provide that in the logs — avg tokens per request ~180, conversational sessions sometimes longer.
04:02 Priya: Note about model variants — you may start on a general-purpose open model from our catalog, then switch to a quantized variant for Dedicated to reduce cost. We can show cost delta in a follow-up spreadsheet.
04:16 Maya: Any competitors or alternatives we should be aware of from your perspective?
04:20 Alex: Customers sometimes evaluate OpenAI (hosted) and Anthropic and also AWS SageMaker for self-hosted endpoints. We can share a short comparison doc.
04:29 Maya: Good. On compliance: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, data retention policy, and the ability to configure retention windows for logs.
04:38 Sam: We'll attach SOC 2 cert and our retention options. For Private you can set retention and we can forward audit logs to your SIEM via syslog/s3.
04:50 Priya: On the network side, we'll need one static egress IP for the Private control plane, and we'll provide a list for firewall rules. For Dedicated, it's in-region infra but we'll also provide IP ranges.
05:03 Jonas: If we do VPC peering, what about DNS and route tables?
05:07 Priya: We'll include route table guidance in the network prep doc. Also, if you have strict egress restrictions we can support a proxy setup.
05:15 Lena: Who will be our day-to-day contact if blockers appear?
05:18 Sam: I'll be your CSM primary contact for onboarding and escalations. Priya will be SE for technical work; Alex for contract and pricing.
05:27 Alex: Billing and procurement — any timelines?
05:29 Lena: We'll need procurement to review pilot T&Cs; won't sign a long contract until we have pilot results.
05:34 Alex: That's standard. We'll provide a pilot quote and a Dedicated estimate after benchmarking.
05:38 Maya: Questions about SSO — we run OKTA. Your SSO flow ok?
05:42 Sam: Yes, we support SAML/Okta SSO for admin consoles, we'll share setup steps.
05:48 Jonas: Any known limitations for on-prem air-gapped? We might explore that long-term.
05:53 Priya: On-prem package exists but is more involved — requires more lead time and an enterprise agreement; we can outline the steps if you want to evaluate later.
06:03 Maya: For the pilot, what telemetry will you need? Raw logs, token counts, latency histograms?
06:09 Priya: Ideally: sample requests/responses (anonymized), token counts, latencies per request, and any error traces. We'll provide a template.
06:17 Alex: Recap of next steps — Alex send onboarding guide + pricing estimate; Priya share network prep + perf template and schedule deep-dive; Sam provision sandbox and invite users; Maya/Jonas share scrubbed logs and QPS numbers.
06:33 Maya: Sounds good. Anything else?
06:36 Lena: No, thanks. Looking forward to the pilot.
06:38 Alex: Great — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive and send docs by end of week. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription occasionally mis-labels acronyms (e.g., "V P C" or "KV cash"). Some crosstalk at 00:25 and short pauses.
